The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the emotional arc of the narrative. The author uses **compression of time** early on, summarizing the previous six weeks of the residency into just two paragraphs to quickly establish the history and unspoken tension between Nell and Arjun. The narrative then slows down to focus on the events of a single afternoon at the beach, allowing the dialogue and atmosphere to breathe. 

During the climax on the beach—when they wade through the water and collapse on the sand—time is subtly **stretched** to focus on sensory details (the cold water, the grit of sand between their palms, the dripping recorder) and Nell's internal realization about why she won't confess her feelings. Finally, the story uses **compression** again at the end, briskly summarizing their rescue, the final dinner, the morning departure, and a jump forward of three months into a few short paragraphs. This mimics the feeling of a fleeting summer romance coming to an abrupt, inevitable end, leaving only a lingering memory.
